records.name: Mantua Worldwide Community
records.summary: Neighbors in Mantua who clean up streets, plant gardens and teach young people how things grow. The group also hosts arts and health events.
records.what_you_do: Show up for a neighborhood cleanup or greenup, join the Garden Club (open to youth and adults), or buy a ticket to a garden party.

schedule.text: About four to six cleanups a year, with dates passed to volunteers. The Garden Club has no meeting day or time posted yet.

cost.text: The site lists no fee for cleanups or the Garden Club. Some events, such as the garden party, charge a ticket.

first_step.how: Send a question through the Contact Us form on mantuaworldwide.com about the next cleanup and the Garden Club start date.
first_step.basis: The Garden Club welcomes youth and adults and takes RSVPs, but its start date is not set yet, and cleanup dates go only to volunteers. The way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Garden Club is described as a place to plant flowers, herbs and vegetables and learn about gardening, and youth and adults are welcome. Its date, time and place were still to be set when we checked, so the site cannot yet say what a visit involves. Cleanups work the streets and gardens of Mantua, and the site does not say how long they run or what volunteers should bring.
first_visit_tips: Ask which cleanup comes next and where volunteers meet, since the site gives no address for cleanups.
Watch the Garden Club page for a start date, because none is set yet.
Use the Contact Us form, since the site lists no general phone number or email.

records.notes: Deep pass. The Garden Club page gives no date, time or place yet, has an RSVP button, and says youth and adults are welcome. The Contact Us page has a form only, with no general phone or email. The garden party is invitation only with a $25 ticket, so it is kept out of the cost text because it is a one-time event. The Garden Club page shows a named person's personal email; it is not copied here, since the Contact Us form is the group's own route. The May events on the event list show no year. The June 2026 Rooted in Wellness item gives no posting date, so the status date stays at the February 2026 article. The site has no volunteering page.

records.name: ManUpPHL
records.summary: A mentoring program that works with young men in Philadelphia who are at high risk of gun violence. Mentoring is open to young men from age 13, with a stipend, and local adults can volunteer as mentors.
records.what_you_do: Young men can ask for help through the Help Now request form. Volunteer mentors can call, email or use the volunteer form.

cost.text: Free to take part. Participants receive a stipend of $15 an hour and a free meal each day.

first_step.how: Young men: send a request through the Help Now form on manupphl.org. Volunteer mentors: call 267-748-7818 or fill in the volunteer form on the site.
first_step.basis: Participants and mentors both start with a form or a call. The site does not describe what happens after the form or what a first meeting looks like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Participants apply, then get a mentor and a support team. The programs page describes sessions on the causes of gun violence, life skills, money management and job readiness, plus a group session led by a licensed therapist. It does not say how long the program runs or what the first session is like.
first_visit_tips: Have your questions ready for the first call, since the site does not describe the first meeting.
Mentor applicants choose a volunteer type and the areas they can help with, such as jobs, education, or family support.
The site lists no walk-in hours, so start with the form or a phone call.

records.notes: Deep pass on the programs, volunteer form, events and news pages. Status is set to dormant under the status rule: the newest dated item on the group's own site is an October 7, 2023 fundraiser, the news page has no dates, and the events page lists nothing upcoming. A search found nothing dated 2026. The help and volunteer forms still work as far as the site shows, so please review before this goes live. Other public listings in search results give different age and stipend figures, so the record uses the group's own programs page (ages 13 to 35, $15 an hour). The homepage also names a three-week adult program for ages up to 35 that the programs page does not describe. The footer copyright (2022 to 2023) is not counted as evidence.

records.name: Mariposa Food Co-op
records.summary: A member-owned natural foods store on Baltimore Avenue in West Philadelphia. Members buy in with a one-time equity payment, get a vote in the co-op's decisions, and can give a few hours a month as working members.
records.what_you_do: Members buy in with equity and vote on co-op decisions. Working members help run the store through shifts or committee service on governance, policy, or education and outreach, and get a 10 percent discount. The co-op says it is restarting the working-member program, so ask before you plan on shifts.

schedule.text: Working members are asked to give at least four hours a month. The store is open every day from 8 am to 9 pm.

locations.label: Store
locations.transit: Served by the 34 trolley and the 64 bus. The site does not name stops.

cost.text: One-time $200 member equity, refundable when you leave (the co-op may hold back refunds to protect its finances). You can start with $50, $75 or more and pay $25 or more every three months until you reach $200. People who qualify can join through Food For All.

access.notes: The site says the store is handicap accessible. It gives no details on ramps, aisles or doors.

first_step.how: Visit the store at 4824 Baltimore Avenue or join online, then pay the $200 equity in one payment or in installments.
first_step.basis: Anyone can shop in the store, and the join steps and payment plans are published. Voting and working roles need membership first.
first_step.what_to_expect: Stop by to look around and ask a staff member how joining works. Joining means filling out an application, either in the store, online, or on a printed form, and paying the member equity. Working members are asked to give at least four hours a month and get training before their first shifts, but the co-op says it is restarting that program.
first_visit_tips: The store is open every day from 8 am to 9 pm, so you can visit at most times.
Ask whether the working-member program is taking new people right now.
If the $200 is hard to pay at once, ask about the installment plan or the Food For All option.

records.notes: Deep pass on the join, working-member, location and events pages. The working-member page says the program is being restarted, so shift details may change. Store hours come from the location page. The access note is only the site's words, handicap accessible, with no detail. The site names the 34 trolley and 64 bus but no stop, so no nearest stop is recorded. The join and events pages carry a 2017 footer; footers are not evidence, so the status stays probably_active with no dated item. The events page lists no events.

records.name: Masjid al-Jamia
records.summary: A masjid in West Philadelphia that teaches Quran recitation with tajweed, tafsir, hadith and practical fiqh, and runs a children's Islamic school. It also has youth programs and weekly tafsir and hadith circles.
records.what_you_do: Join a weekly tafsir or hadith circle, enroll children in the Islamic school, or come to a family event with talks, halal food stalls and children's activities. The site gives no date for the family event.

schedule.text: Weekly tafsir and hadith circles and Quran classes are listed, but the site gives no days or times for them. Friday prayer with a sermon is held weekly. Prayer times appear only in images on the site.

access.notes: Sermons are given in Arabic with an English translation.

first_step.how: Call (267) 275-8087 to ask about the next tafsir or hadith circle and the children's Islamic school, since the site gives no class times.
first_step.basis: The site says its programs are for all ages and gives a phone line and a contact form. It does not give class times, costs or registration steps, and two of its forms link nowhere.
first_step.what_to_expect: The mosque is in the former Commodore Theatre building on Walnut Street. It was founded in 1988 by members of a university Muslim students group and serves a diverse congregation. The circles cover Quran commentary and the Prophet's sayings, and the children's school teaches Quran, Arabic and Islamic character. The site does not say how long sessions run or what they cost, so the phone call is the best first step.
first_visit_tips: Call (267) 275-8087 before you come, because the site gives no visiting hours.
The Friday sermon is given in Arabic with an English translation.
The mosque is at 4228 Walnut Street in West Philadelphia.

records.notes: Deep pass on the services, announcement, about and home pages. The only dated item is an announcement of weekly tafsir and hadith circles for August 22 to 24, 2025, which sets the status date. The services page gives no days, times, fees or registration steps for classes, the Islamic school or prayers. The Become a Muslim and Ask a question forms link nowhere. The family event on the homepage is undated and was not used as evidence. The 2026 copyright and the founding year (1988) are not evidence of current activity.

records.name: Masjid Mujahideen
records.summary: A masjid on South 60th Street that runs social services, spiritual education, and a Jawala Scouts program for young men focused on life skills and outdoor training.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer, take part in the social services, join the Jawala Scouts, or donate. The site invites people to get involved but does not name volunteer roles, so ask by phone or email.

schedule.text: The site lists no meeting days or times for the Jawala Scouts or the social services.

cost.text: The site lists no fee for volunteering or the Jawala Scouts. Some community events sell tickets, and donations can be made in person or online.

first_step.how: Call (215) 471-7073 and ask how to join the Jawala Scouts or start volunteering, since the site names no volunteer roles.
first_step.basis: The site invites visitors to volunteer and lists the Jawala Scouts, but it gives no ages, meeting times or sign-up steps for either.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Jawala Scouts are described as a network of Muslim men who mentor young men, teaching riding, swimming, shooting, wrestling and small business skills through outdoor experiences. The site does not say when or where sessions meet, what the ages are, or what it costs. Ask about those details before you come, because the site gives none of them.
first_visit_tips: Call before you visit, since the site gives no meeting times or ages for the scouts.
The email on the contact page shows one address but links to another, so the phone may be the safer route.
The masjid is at 413 South 60th Street.

records.notes: Deep pass on the home, Jawala Scouts, support, contact and events pages. The events page lists no events and only says community events are coming, without naming any. The newest dated item is the youth fundraising gala on December 27, 2024, which sets the status date. The 2024 footer copyright is not counted. The contact page shows admin@ but the link behind it goes to a different Gmail address, and one email on the donation page is misspelled. Confirm the current address before publishing contact details. The Jawala Scouts page gives no ages, meeting place or cost. No volunteer roles are named.

records.name: Masjidullah
records.summary: A mosque on Limekiln Pike with Friday prayer and programs for families. The site also lists health and human services and Ramadan programs, and links to a child care center and a learning institute on their own sites.
records.what_you_do: Attend Friday prayer at 1:15 pm, sign up to volunteer through the site, ask the office about the child care center and the New Medina Institute, or ask about the free grocery bags through Health and Human Services for people with low or no income.

schedule.text: Friday prayer is held every week at 1:15 pm. The site also lists a Sunday Islam 101 class at 10 am and a Monday evening Seerah series from Maghrib to Isha. Cost and enrollment for the classes are not stated.

cost.text: The site gives no fee for Friday prayer or the listed classes. The grocery bags from Health and Human Services are free.

first_step.how: Call the office at 215-621-7800 or email inquiries@masjidullah.org to ask whether visitors can join Friday prayer or the Sunday Islam 101 class.
first_step.basis: The site sends people to membership and volunteer forms and does not say whether visitors can attend Friday prayer or the classes. A phone line and an email address are listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Friday prayer is held every week at 1:15 pm at the mosque on Limekiln Pike, and the site lists a Sunday Islam 101 class and a Monday evening Seerah series. The site does not describe what visitors should do, how long sessions last, or what they cost. The office can answer those questions before you come.
first_visit_tips: The business office is open Monday to Thursday, 10 am to 4 pm, and Friday, 9 am to 1 pm, so call during those hours.
Ask about the Islam 101 class cost and sign-up before you come, since the site lists neither.
The grocery program lists no application steps, so call the office to ask how to get a bag.

records.notes: Deep pass on the home, services, groups, events and Health and Human Services pages. The footer copyright is 2017. The events page has only flyer images with no readable dates, so no status date is set and the 2025 in an image file name is not used. Friday prayer and the two classes come from the services page, which is undated. Membership and volunteer sign-up are external forms; they were not opened or filled in. The groups page lists one private group with one member, so it is not recorded. Health and Human Services gives a free grocery bag, is described as a registered emergency food cupboard, and serves people with low or no income in Philadelphia. MECCA Child Care and the New Medina Learning Institute are separate organizations with their own sites, listed in leads_only.

records.name: Maternity B.V.M. Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish on Old Bustleton Avenue in the Northeast with five Sunday Masses, weekday morning Masses, a Saturday vigil Mass at 4:30 pm, and Saturday confession from 3 to 4 pm.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass or to confession. Call the rectory to ask about faith formation and parish groups, since the archdiocese page lists no parish groups.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8, 9:30 and 11 am, and at 12:30 and 7 pm. Saturday vigil Mass at 4:30 pm and Saturday Mass at 8 am. Weekday Masses at 6:30 and 8 am in the lower chapel. Saturday confession from 3 to 4 pm in the lower chapel. An Old Church Mass at 10:30 am on the first Sunday of the month from October to December and April to June.

access.notes: The archdiocese page says the church has accessible entrances, ramps and wide doors, accessible parking with van space, and wheelchair-accessible restrooms.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass, then call the rectory at 215-673-8127 to ask about faith formation and parish groups.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone and a phone number is listed. The archdiocese page names no parish groups or newcomer program, so the way into a group is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, with five Sunday Masses and a Saturday vigil at 4:30 pm. Weekday Masses are held in the lower chapel, and Saturday confession runs from 3 to 4 pm in the same room. The archdiocese page names a Director of Religious Education but no other parish groups, so ask the rectory who runs faith formation.
first_visit_tips: The archdiocese page notes accessible entrances, ramps and van-accessible parking.
The Old Church Mass is only held on the first Sunday of certain months, so check the time before you go.
Confession is on Saturdays from 3 to 4 pm in the lower chapel.

records.notes: The parish's own website returned HTTP 403, so every deep detail here comes from the Archdiocese of Philadelphia parish page. The tier 1 summary called the confession hour an evening hour; the archdiocese page gives 3 to 4 pm, so the summary is corrected. The parish school at 9322 Old Bustleton Ave. is a school, not a community group, and is not recorded. The archdiocese page also lists a second rectory line, 215-676-5144. Status is probably_active because the Mass schedule is an ongoing published service and the page has no dated items; its 2026 footer is not counted.

leads_only.name: MECCA Child Care
leads_only.note: Islamic early childhood center at 7401 Limekiln Pike, named on the Masjidullah site. Fetched 2026-10-08: infant, toddler, preschool and school-age programs plus summer camp. Hours, tuition and enrollment steps are not stated. A separate organization outside this batch, so it is left for future research.

leads_only.name: New Medina Learning Institute
leads_only.note: Learning school at 7401 Limekiln Pike, 2nd floor, named on the Masjidullah site as the New Medina Institute. Fetched 2026-10-08: programs are listed by name only, with no ages, class times or costs. The latest dated item is a February 2023 showcase and the footer reads 2023. A separate organization outside this batch, so it is left for future research.

blocked.note: HTTP 403 on the homepage fetch. Not retried or worked around. Parish details come from the Archdiocese of Philadelphia parish page instead.

notes: Seven groups read. 31 fetches used of 42 allowed (up to 6 per group, plus two leads). 1 of 1 WebSearch used, to check ManUpPHL for 2026 activity; it found nothing dated 2026. ManUpPHL is set to dormant under the status rule (newest dated item on its own site is October 2023), so please review before it goes live. Mariposa says its working-member program is restarting. The Maternity B.V.M. website returned 403 and is listed under blocked. No rate limiting was seen. One search result carried a formatting instruction aimed at the reply; it was search text and was not acted on.
